questions.typeHeader: TYPE - I: SINGLE DIE OUTCOMES
questions.questionText: A fair die is thrown once. What is the probability of obtaining an even number?
questions.solution: Even numbers on a die: $\{2, 4, 6\} \implies 3$ outcomes out of 6. Probability $= \frac{3}{6} = \frac{1}{2}$.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - I: SINGLE DIE OUTCOMES

questions.solution: Favorable outcomes: numbers $> 4 \implies 2$ outcomes out of 6. Probability $= \frac{2}{6}$.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: STANDARD DECK OF 52 CARDS
questions.questionText: A card is drawn at random from a well-shuffled pack of $52$ cards. What is the probability of drawing a Queen?
questions.solution: There are 4 Queens in a pack of 52. Probability $= \frac{4}{52} = \frac{1}{13}$.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: STANDARD DECK OF 52 CARDS
questions.questionText: One card is drawn from a pack of $52$ cards. Find the probability of getting a King of red color.
questions.solution: Red Kings are Hearts and Diamonds (2 cards). Probability $= \frac{2}{52} = \frac{1}{26}$.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - III: STANDARD DECK OF 52 CARDS

questions.solution: There are 12 face cards (J, Q, K of 4 suits). Probability $= \frac{12}{52} = \frac{3}{13}$.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - V: COIN TOSSING (MULTIPLE COINS)
questions.questionText: Three unbiased coins are tossed together. Find the probability of getting at least two heads.
questions.solution: Total outcomes $= 2^3 = 8$. Outcomes with $\ge 2$ heads: HHH, HHT, HTH, THH (4 outcomes). Probability $= \frac{4}{8} = \frac{1}{2}$.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - V: COIN TOSSING (MULTIPLE COINS)
questions.questionText: Two coins are tossed simultaneously. What is the probability of getting exactly one Head?
questions.solution: Outcomes: HH, HT, TH, TT (4 outcomes). Exactly one head: HT, TH (2 outcomes). Probability $= \frac{2}{4} = \frac{1}{2}$.

questions.solution: Outcomes: HH, HT, TH, TT (4 outcomes). Exactly one head: HT, TH (2 outcomes). Probability $= \frac{2}{4} = \frac{1}{2}$.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - V: COIN TOSSING (MULTIPLE COINS)
questions.questionText: Three unbiased coins are tossed together. Find the probability of getting at least two heads.
questions.solution: Total outcomes $= 2^3 = 8$. Outcomes with $\ge 2$ heads: HHH, HHT, HTH, THH (4 outcomes). Probability $= \frac{4}{8} = \frac{1}{2}$.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VI: CALENDAR & LEAP YEAR PROBABILITY
questions.questionText: What is the probability that a leap year selected at random contains $53$ Sundays?
questions.solution: A leap year has 366 days $= 52$ weeks $+ 2$ odd days. The 2 odd days can be (Sun,Mon), (Mon,Tue), ... (Sat,Sun). 2 pairs contain Sunday out of 7. Probability $= \frac{2}{7}$.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VI: CALENDAR & LEAP YEAR PROBABILITY
questions.questionText: Find the probability that a non-leap year has $53$ Mondays.
questions.solution: A normal year has 365 days $= 52$ weeks $+ 1$ odd day. 1 out of 7 days is Monday. Probability $= \frac{1}{7}$.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VII: INDEPENDENT EVENTS
questions.questionText: Two persons A and B shoot at a target independently. The probability of A hitting the target is $\frac{2}{5}$ and that of B is $\frac{3}{6}$. Find the probability that both hit the target.
questions.solution: $P(A \cap B) = P(A) \times P(B) = \frac{2}{5} \times \frac{3}{6} = \frac{6}{30} = \frac{1}{5}$.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VII: INDEPENDENT EVENTS
questions.questionText: Two persons A and B shoot at a target independently. The probability of A hitting the target is $\frac{3}{5}$ and that of B is $\frac{4}{6}$. Find the probability that both hit the target.
questions.solution: $P(A \cap B) = P(A) \times P(B) = \frac{3}{5} \times \frac{4}{6} = \frac{12}{30} = \frac{2}{5}$.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VII: INDEPENDENT EVENTS
questions.questionText: Two persons A and B shoot at a target independently. The probability of A hitting the target is $\frac{4}{5}$ and that of B is $\frac{5}{6}$. Find the probability that both hit the target.
questions.solution: $P(A \cap B) = P(A) \times P(B) = \frac{4}{5} \times \frac{5}{6} = \frac{20}{30} = \frac{2}{3}$.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - VIII: COMPLEMENTARY PROBABILITY (AT LEAST ONE)
questions.questionText: The probability of a student passing an examination is $\frac{1}{5}$. What is the probability that the student fails the examination?
questions.solution: $P(\text{Fail}) = 1 - P(\text{Pass}) = 1 - \frac{1}{5} = \frac{4}{5}$.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - I: SINGLE DIE OUTCOMES
questions.questionText: A fair die is rolled once. What is the probability of getting a number strictly greater than $2$?
questions.solution: Favorable outcomes: numbers $> 2 \implies 4$ outcomes out of 6. Probability $= \frac{4}{6}$.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - I: SINGLE DIE OUTCOMES
questions.questionText: A fair die is thrown once. What is the probability of obtaining an even number?
questions.solution: Even numbers on a die: $\{2, 4, 6\} \implies 3$ outcomes out of 6. Probability $= \frac{3}{6} = \frac{1}{2}$.

questions.typeHeader: TYPE - I: SINGLE DIE OUTCOMES
questions.questionText: A fair die is rolled once. What is the probability of getting a number strictly greater than $4$?
questions.solution: Favorable outcomes: numbers $> 4 \implies 2$ outcomes out of 6. Probability $= \frac{2}{6}$.
